Patient Laura Mancini
 The patient, 50 years old, comes to the consultation due to thin hair, everted eyelid, history of basal cell cancer and axillary ephelides. She reports noticing a decrease in hair density and changes in the texture of her hair in recent months. In addition, she reports discomfort in her eyelids and skin lesions in the armpits.

 Thin and sparse hair, everted eyelids, characteristic lesions of basal cell cancer on the skin and ephelides in the armpits are observed. The rest of the physical examination is within normal parameters.

 A possible dermatological condition is suspected that may be affecting both the scalp and the skin of the patient. Complementary studies are required for a definitive diagnosis.

 A biopsy of the skin lesions is indicated for histopathological study, a complete blood test and a consultation with a dermatologist for evaluation and follow-up.

The patient is given an appointment for a review of the results and therapeutic plan.

The patient, aged 45, comes to the consultation due to a clinical picture characterized by a chronic recurrent brain disorder, lack of ossification of the humeral epiphysis, optic drusen, triangular epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the fourth finger of the hand, chondrocalcinosis and phalangeal sclerosis of the fourth finger of the hand.


The patient reports previous episodes of joint pain in the hands and difficulty with mobility.


The physical examination reveals the presence of deformities in the phalanges of the hands, as well as limitation in their mobility. Likewise, the presence of optic drusen is evident in the ophthalmological examination.


The possibility of a genetic disorder affecting the connective tissue is raised, which would explain the symptoms presented by the patient.


Genetic studies will be carried out to confirm the diagnosis and symptomatic treatment will be prescribed to improve the patient's quality of life.

A check-up is scheduled in one month to monitor progress.

Specialist in Internal Medicine
Patient Beatrice Messina

The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that have been progressing in recent weeks.

Medical History
The patient reports having experienced difficulty walking in a coordinated manner, as well as episodes of loss of bladder control at night. In addition, she has noticed a decrease in her visual acuity and has been previously diagnosed with ovarian agenesis.


On physical examination, physiological anisocoria, posterior polar cataract in both eyes, and signs of gait ataxia are observed. Urethral obstruction is also evident, and pulmonary heterotaxia with bilateral trilobed lungs is suspected.

Studies Performed
An EEG was performed which showed generalized polymorphic epileptiform activity.


Based on the symptoms presented by the patient, the findings of the physical examination and the studies performed, the diagnosis of a possible neurological disease with ophthalmological, urogenital and pulmonary manifestations is proposed.


Pharmacological treatment will be started to control the epileptic seizures and the patient will be referred to specialists in neurology, ophthalmology and urology for comprehensive management of her condition.

Periodic check-ups are scheduled for follow-up and treatment adjustment.

Patient Saverio Russo

The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that have been appearing progressively in recent months.

Personal history
The patient does not report any relevant medical history, except for an episode of fracture in the bones of the forearm 2 years ago, which was treated conservatively.


After the clinical evaluation, several significant findings have been identified. The patient presents Leber's optic neuropathy, malformation of the epididymis, neurological dysfunction, osteoarthritis of the distal interphalangeal joint, papillary renal carcinoma and mandibular hypoplasia.


A genetic disorder affecting multiple body systems is suspected, which would explain the variety of symptoms present in the patient. Genetic studies are required to confirm the diagnosis.

Management plan
Specific genetic tests will be performed to identify the mutation responsible for the symptoms present in the patient. A consultation with the genetics service will also be arranged for advice and follow-up.

Next appointment
The patient is scheduled for a review of results and follow-up planning within a period of 4 weeks.

Tests performed

The patient is scheduled for a check-up in one month.

After performing a brain MRI, the presence of a spindle cell tumor in the pituitary gland is identified, which could be related to the Horton-type headache reported by the patient. Likewise, the presence of acute myelomonocytic leukemia is evident in the blood tests performed.

5. Atypical inflammation

 Hypergrowth of long bones in a pediatric patient. Radiological studies will be performed to evaluate the degree of hyperdevelopment and rule out possible underlying causes.

Patient Paola Monti
 2-year-old patient with a history of delayed eruption of baby teeth and an undeveloped nose. She has immobility of the small joints of the foot, abnormal epiphyses of the second toe, ventricular dysrhythmias, atonic epilepsy, and polymorphic focal epileptiform discharges. Radiological and electroencephalographic studies are performed to evaluate the patient's current condition.

 Absence of mobility in the affected joints, delayed teething, small nose, and abnormalities in the epiphyses of the second toe are observed. Episodes of disorientation and loss of consciousness are evident.

 A rare genetic disorder affecting bone, dental, and neurological development is suspected. Specialized follow-up is required for comprehensive and multidisciplinary treatment.

 Symptomatic treatment is started to control the seizures and the patient is referred to genetics for molecular study.

Neurology Specialist
Patient Antonella Farina
 The patient, a 35-year-old woman, comes to the doctor's office due to episodes of weakness on one side of the body, accompanied by gait disturbances and recurrent headaches. In addition, a decrease in proteins in the amniotic fluid has been observed during pregnancy.

 After performing various diagnostic tests, the presence of brain malformations has been detected, specifically a malformation of the cranial vault, as well as hyperplasia of the fibula. Ischemic changes have also been identified in the electrocardiogram.

 Based on the symptoms presented and the clinical findings, the diagnosis of a rare medical condition known as MoyaMoya Syndrome is established, which is characterized by the progressive obstruction of the internal carotid arteries, which can cause episodes of intermittent hemiplegia and alterations in cerebral circulation.

 A multidisciplinary treatment will be started that will include the administration of drugs to improve cerebral blood circulation, as well as physiotherapy sessions to improve muscle weakness.

Periodic check-ups are scheduled to evaluate the patient's progress and make adjustments to the treatment if necessary.

Patient Giuseppe Martinelli

The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to symptoms that suggest a complex clinical picture. Among the most relevant findings are the presence of a ventricular apex towards the midline, a tendency to fall, a dense epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the second toe, abdominal muscle deficit, mesomelic brachydactyly, bone cystic hemangiomatosis, and eyelid ptosis.


On physical examination, the presence of mesomelic brachydactyly is observed, as well as a dense epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the second toe. In addition, an abdominal muscle deficit and bilateral eyelid ptosis are evident. Regarding complementary studies, a brain MRI has been performed that shows a ventricular apex displaced towards the midline.


After the clinical evaluation and the studies carried out, the possibility of Gorlin-Goltz syndrome is raised, a rare genetic disease characterized by the presence of multiple bone cysts, hemangiomas, brachydactyly and other clinical manifestations.


A multidisciplinary follow-up will be carried out with specialists in genetics, neurology and orthopedics, in order to establish a comprehensive management plan for the patient.

Patient Diego Sorrentino
 The patient, 45 years old, comes to the outpatient clinic due to pain and inflammation in the joint of the big toe of the left foot, as well as the presence of a lump on the nail of the same foot. In addition, she reports stiffness and pain when trying to move the left shoulder in flexion.

 On physical examination, a malformation of the epiphyses of the left hallux, a nail tumor on the big toe of the left foot and stiffness in the joint of the left shoulder in flexion are observed.

 Based on the symptoms and clinical findings described, the differential diagnosis of osteoarthritis in the joint of the big toe of the left foot, onychomycosis in the nail of the same toe and adhesive capsulitis in the joint of the left shoulder is raised.

 Pharmacological treatment is indicated for pain and inflammation, as well as complementary studies to confirm the proposed diagnoses.

The patient is given an appointment for follow-up and evaluation of results.

Outpatient Consultation Report

Patient 
Date of Birth 03/15/1980
Date of Consultation 05/02/2022


The patient comes to the outpatient clinic due to chronic gastrointestinal symptoms, such as abdominal distension, severe constipation, difficulty feeding, and involuntary weight loss. In addition, he reports a history of delayed psychomotor development since childhood.

Clinical Findings
On physical examination, a distended abdomen is observed on palpation, without the presence of masses or megacolon. The patient presents signs of malnutrition and growth retardation. No other relevant findings are evident on physical examination.

Studies Performed
Radiological studies were performed that showed signs of dilation of intestinal loops and chronic constipation. In addition, genetic tests were carried out which confirmed the presence of mutations associated with Hirschsprung's disease and Refsum's disease.


1. Hirschsprung's disease
2. Refsum's disease

Treatment plan
Multidisciplinary treatment will be initiated with a gastroenterologist, nutritionist and geneticist to comprehensively address the complications associated with both diseases. Close follow-up will be carried out to monitor the patient's clinical progress.

Patient Alessio Benedetti
 The patient, 8 years old, comes to the consultation due to bilateral ulnar hypoplasia, facial hypotrichosis, and hip deformity. Ulnar hypoplasia is manifested by the presence of a shorter than normal forearm, with limited pronation and supination. Facial hypotrichosis is characterized by a lack of hair on the face, especially on the eyebrows and eyelashes. Regarding the hip deformity, an asymmetry in the length of the lower limbs and difficulty walking are observed.

 The examination reveals the presence of bilateral ulnar hypoplasia, facial hypotrichosis, and limited mobility of the right hip.

 Differential diagnosis is made between several entities, including Holt-Oram Syndrome, Wolf-Hirschhorn Syndrome, Cleidocranial Dysplasia, Campomelic Dysplasia and Thanatophoric Dysplasia.

 Genetic studies will be requested to confirm the diagnosis and the start of a multidisciplinary treatment that includes orthopedics, genetics and physiotherapy will be considered.

A check-up is scheduled in one month to monitor and control the evolution of the symptoms.

The patient has no relevant medical history. He does not report recent trauma or previous surgeries.

A jaw x-ray and a testicular ultrasound are requested to evaluate the possible causes of the symptoms presented.

These include phalangeal sclerosis of the fourth toe, hypoplasia of the epiphysis of the second toe, weakness in the extensors of the big toe, asymmetry of the auricle, anomaly of the skeletal system, and verbal dyspraxia. These symptoms have been progressing in recent months, which has caused concern in the patient.

 During the physical examination, the presence of sclerosis in the distal phalanx of the fourth toe of the left foot is observed, as well as hypoplasia of the epiphysis of the second toe of the right hand.  After the evaluation of the symptoms and the physical examination, the possibility arises that the patient has a rare genetic disease that affects multiple systems of the body, including the skeletal system and the nervous system. Additional genetic studies are required to confirm the diagnosis.

 Close monitoring of the patient will be initiated and genetic testing will be coordinated to identify the underlying cause of the symptoms. A multidisciplinary approach will be considered, including specialists in genetics, neurology and orthopedics.

The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to hypertrophy of the wrists, itchy skin and a disorder of the skeletal system. He reports that the hypertrophy of the wrists has been progressive in recent months, accompanied by bone discomfort and generalized itching.


There is an increase in volume in both wrists, red and flaky skin, as well as limitation of joint mobility. On palpation, pain is noted in the bone region of the wrists. No other relevant findings are evident in the physical examination.

Studies performed
X-rays of the wrists have been performed, which show signs of hyperostosis in the carpal region. In addition, blood tests have been requested to rule out possible metabolic causes of hypertrophy.


The patient has a condition of diffuse idiopathic hyperostosis, which manifests itself with bone hypertrophy in the wrists, itching and joint discomfort. Follow-up by the rheumatology service is required to monitor the evolution of the disease.


Symptomatic treatment for the itching is indicated, as well as physical therapy to improve joint mobility. Periodic follow-up is scheduled to assess the response to the treatment and make adjustments as necessary.

 The patient, a 45-year-old man, comes to the consultation presenting a complex clinical picture. He reports chronic abdominal pain, alterations in urination and a history of recurrent respiratory tract infections. In addition, the physical examination shows the presence of acquired microcephaly and signs of autonomic dysfunction.

Complementary examinations Imaging tests have been performed that reveal the presence of polycystic renal dysplasia and abdominal hernia. In addition, laboratory tests show a NAGT deficiency.

 After evaluating the symptoms and the results of the tests performed, the diagnosis of nodular granulomatous vasculitis is established. This rare disease affects multiple organs and explains the symptoms presented by the patient.

 Immunosuppressive treatment will be started to control vasculitis, in addition to measures for the management of renal dysplasia and abdominal hernia.

Follow-up The patient will be monitored periodically in consultation to evaluate the response to treatment and make adjustments as necessary.

 The patient comes to the consultation due to a disorder in the regulation of transition cations, which has caused the appearance of a hammer on the second toe. The patient reports pain and inflammation in the affected area.

 Upon examination, a deformity is observed in the second toe with redness, local heat and functional limitation. In addition, signs of inflammation are evident in the metatarsophalangeal joint.

Patient Tiziana Ferrara

The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation because she has been experiencing symptoms for several months that include allergic reactions after eating food, eye problems, and hand malformations.


The patient has a history of allergy to cow's milk protein diagnosed in childhood. In addition, the presence of vitreous amyloidosis has been observed in previous ophthalmological studies. On the other hand, agenesis of the distal phalanx of the thumb of the right hand has been detected in recent x-rays.


On examination, redness of the skin is observed, especially in the facial area, after eating dairy products. Likewise, an accumulation of amyloid material is evident in the vitreous humor of the right eye, which coincides with previous findings. In the right hand, the absence of the distal phalanx of the thumb is noted, with limitation in the mobility of said joint.


1. Allergy to cow's milk protein.
2. Vitreous amyloidosis.
3. Agenesis of the distal phalanx of the thumb of the right hand.


The patient is recommended to avoid the consumption of dairy products and to follow a diet free of cow's milk protein. Regarding vitreous amyloidosis, periodic ophthalmological follow-up is suggested. Regarding the malformation in the hand, the possibility of surgical intervention will be assessed in case of significant functional limitation.

This report is issued at the request of the patient for medical follow-up.

The patient, aged 55, comes to the consultation presenting difficulty swallowing, generalised amyloid deposits in the skin, spontaneous bruising, narrowing in the proximal part of the metacarpals, recurrent abdominal pain and episodes of bradycardia.

Tests performed
Various studies have been carried out, including a skin biopsy which has confirmed the presence of amyloid deposits. In addition, a disorder in platelet aggregation and alterations in the gallbladder have been observed.


After analysing the symptoms and the results of the tests, the diagnosis of Systemic Amyloidosis is established, a rare disease characterised by the accumulation of amyloid proteins in different tissues and organs of the body.


A specific treatment for Systemic Amyloidosis will be started, which will include therapies to reduce the production of amyloid proteins and control the present symptoms.

Periodic check-ups are scheduled to evaluate the response to the treatment and make adjustments as necessary.

 On physical examination, hallux varus, honeycomb palmoplantar keratoderma, short fingers, primary ciliary dyskinesia, and signs of basal ganglia dysfunction are observed. In addition, instability when walking and spontaneous falls are evident.

The patient has no relevant medical history.
